verdicts.reason: The two candidates use the same three-column layout, which reads correctly left to right. In A, the stained-glass window fills almost the full height and nearly touches the top and bottom edges, the headline sits tight to the left edge, and the address sits tight to the right edge, so it feels cramped. B gives the window and both text blocks a little more margin, which keeps it closer to the original's breathing room. Both share the same flaws: the date and address text is tiny and hard to read at this size, and there is dead space between the columns.
